title: Moving animals — horses & whales
summary: Icelandic horses and surfacing whales: unpredictable, fast, and worth every frame.
why: Moving subjects need three things at once: a shutter floor that freezes motion, an AF system that keeps up, and enough frames to catch the peak. The D7100's AF-C + 3D tracking + 6 fps burst is built for exactly this.

steps.text: Mode dial to S, rear dial to 1/500
Focus-mode switch AF, hold center button, rear dial to AF-C
Hold ISO, enable Auto ISO with the front dial
Release collar to CH — ride the burst at the peak moment

pitfalls: On the whale boat, 1/500s isn't enough — the deck moves too. 1/1000s floor and elbows braced on the rail.
Never feed or crowd the horses for a shot — long lens, calm distance, they'll come to the fence anyway.
levelUp: 1.3× crop mode: 200mm frames like 390mm, burst rises to 7 fps, and the AF points cover the whole frame — the whale-watching cheat code.
